source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. The lost forest when white fog rises and the paths rearrange themselves: eerie, hushed and disorienting, like a half-remembered lullaby heard from the wrong direction. Mysterious and uneasy but still delicate and beautiful, not horror; slow pulse, lots of space. Tempo 72 BPM, 4/4 time, key of D minor. Instrumentation: bowed vibraphone and glass harmonica tones, a music box playing fragments of a folk melody slightly out of reach, low cello drone, sul ponticello violins, distant wooden flute echoes, soft low taiko pulse, rustling rain stick. Form: low drone and fog-like glass tones; music-box fragments; a slow pulse enters under distant flute calls; strings tighten into a quiet unresolved swell; back to the drone and music box. Duration: 110 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
